description: Method A: a global pairwise alignment by Biopython's PairwiseAligner. Every alignment of optimal score is enumerated; the representative is the 3'-most of them.
name: channelscope.m01.align_a

parameters.representative: 3'-most: the latest first gap column, then the latest second, and so on

description: Method B: a global pairwise alignment by parasail's nw_trace, a separately written C library. It scores in integers, so BLOSUM62 and both gap scores are doubled: the same scoring scaled by two, with its score in those units. One optimal alignment, by parasail's own tie-breaking.
name: channelscope.m01.align_b

parameters.substitution_matrix: BLOSUM62 x 2, parasail's own, checked equal to Biopython's on the 400 pairs of standard amino acids

description: Run methods A and B on two numberings, and build the per-column residue mapping from method A's representative alignment: identity in a window, the indel and ambiguity flags, and reliability by the mission's rules.
name: channelscope.m01.build_mapping

parameters.ambiguous: another partner in an alignment of equal score, or in method B's alignment

description: Run M01's pre-registered checks A3-A9 and A11 on the residue mapping, each with an injected fault it must catch.
